sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Ogasawara JAPANESE: quotes Hirayama (1940 survey; 1965: 5) that the accent of people born on Chichijima/Hahajima is 一型 (one-pattern, as on Hachijō). Not about Bonin English.

sources.note: Only segmental remarks (/l/-/r/ distinction and rhotic /r/ acquired by the Navy Generation); no stress statement. Confirms the earlier scan.

sources.citation: 永田高志 (Nagata, Takashi). 2019. 書評: ダニエル・ロング著『小笠原諸島の混合言語の歴史と構造』. 日本語の研究 15(1): 43-50. doi:10.20666/nihongonokenkyu.15.1_43
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: ロング, ダニエル・磯野英治・塚原佑紀 (Long, Daniel, Eiji Isono & Yuki Tsukahara). 2008. 小笠原諸島の欧米系島民に見られる語アクセントの型およびその世代差 [Word-accent patterns of the Ogasawara 'Westerner' islanders and their generational differences]. 小笠原研究年報 (Ogasawara Research Annual Report) 31: 31-40. Tokyo Metropolitan University. hdl:10748/2354
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the JAPANESE pitch accent system of the Westerner islanders, not Bonin English: middle-aged (pre-reversion) speakers are 無型アクセント (accentless, no lexical accent contrast), the young generation is Tokyo-type; accentlessness attributed to English-L1 interference plus the one-pattern Hachijō dialect (pp. 38-39). Nothing on English word stress.

sources.citation: ロング, ダニエル (Long, Daniel). 2005. 『小笠原ことばしゃべる辞典』から [From the Talking Dictionary of the Bonin Islands Language]. 音声研究 (Journal of the Phonetic Society of Japan) 9(3): 37-43. doi:10.24467/onseikenkyu.9.3_37
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §5 音声・音韻関連の項目 (pp. 41-42) discusses syllable structure and segmental pronunciation of island words (baas, droos) and one suprasegmental point: wh-questions in 'Ogasawara kotoba' frequently carry rising intonation, unlike English and Japanese. No statement about word stress.

sources.citation: ロング, ダニエル (Long, Daniel). 1998. 小笠原諸島における言語接触の歴史 [The history of language contact in the Ogasawara Islands]. 日本語研究センター報告 (Reports of the Japanese Language Research Center, Osaka Shoin Women's College) 6: 87-127.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociohistorical account; phonological remarks limited to non-rhoticity (post-vocalic /r/ loss) and Japanese-influenced [tsu] for 'to'. No stress statement.

sources.citation: ロング, ダニエル (ed.). 2002. 日本のもう一つの先住民の危機言語 — 小笠原における欧米系島民の消滅の危機に瀕した英語とその文化 [Another endangered indigenous language of Japan: the endangered English of the Westerner islanders of Ogasawara and their culture]. 科学研究費報告書 (Grant-in-Aid report), Osaka Gakuin University.

sources.note: Unpublished research report specifically on the Westerner islanders' English; likely holds transcribed recordings and phonological notes preceding the 2007 monograph.

Esp. ch. 4 'English before the arrival of Japanese: native and contact varieties' (pp. 39-79), ch. 6 'Late-nineteenth-century Bonin English' (pp. 99-120), ch. 8 (pp. 133-153), ch. 10 '"Navy Generation" Bonin English' (pp. 167-178)
